title.zh: 卷269 列傳五十六 索额图 明珠
title.en: Volume 269 Biographies 56: Suo Etu, Ming Zhu
title.raw: 卷269 列傳五十六 索额图 明珠

sentences.zh: 索額圖明珠-{余國柱}-佛倫

translations.literal: Songgotu, Mingzhu, {Yuguo}, and Folun
translations.idiomatic: Songgotu, Mingzhu, {Yuguo}, and Folun

sentences.zh: 索額圖，赫舍里氏，滿洲正黃旗人，索尼第二子。

translations.literal: Songgotu, of the Heseri clan, was a man of the Manchu Plain Yellow Banner, the second son of Sonin.
translations.idiomatic: Songgotu of the Heseri clan, a Manchu of the Plain Yellow Banner, was Sonin's second son.

sentences.zh: 初授侍衛，自三等洊升一等。

translations.literal: At first he was appointed a guardsman, and was promoted step by step from the third rank to the first rank.
translations.idiomatic: He first entered service as a guardsman and rose successively from third rank to first.

sentences.zh: 康熙七年，授吏部侍郎。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Kangxi, he was appointed Vice Minister of the Board of Civil Appointments.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 7 he was made vice minister of the Board of Civil Appointments.

sentences.zh: 八年五月，自請解任效力左右，復為一等侍衛。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the eighth year, he voluntarily requested to resign his post and serve at the Emperor's side; he was again made a first-rank guardsman.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of Kangxi 8 he asked to leave office and serve at the Emperor's side, and was restored to first-rank guardsman.

sentences.zh: 及鼇拜獲罪，大學士班布爾善坐黨誅，授索額圖國史院大學士，兼佐領。

translations.literal: When Oboi was found guilty, Grand Secretary Banbulishan was executed as a partisan; Songgotu was appointed Grand Secretary of the Historiography Institute, and concurrently served as a company commander.
translations.idiomatic: After Oboi's conviction, Grand Secretary Banbulishan was put to death for factionalism; Songgotu was made grand secretary of the Historiography Institute and given a company command as well.

sentences.zh: 九年，改保和殿大學士。

translations.literal: In the ninth year, he was transferred to Grand Secretary of the Hall of Preserving Harmony.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 9 he became grand secretary of the Hall of Preserving Harmony.

sentences.zh: 十一年，世祖實錄成，加太子太傅。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year, when the Veritable Records of Emperor Shizu were completed, he was given the additional title of Junior Preceptor to the Crown Prince.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 11, upon completion of the Veritable Records of Emperor Shizu, he received the additional title of junior preceptor to the Crown Prince.

sentences.zh: 十五年，大學士熊賜履票本有誤，改寫草簽，既又毀去。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year, Grand Secretary Xiong Cilv's memorial draft contained an error; he rewrote the draft slip, then destroyed it.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 15 Grand Secretary Xiong Cilv's memorial draft was found in error; he rewrote the slip and then destroyed it.

sentences.zh: 索額圖與大學士巴泰、杜立德等疏劾，賜履坐罷歸。

translations.literal: Songgotu, together with Grand Secretaries Batai, Du Lede, and others, submitted a memorial of impeachment; Cilv was dismissed and sent home.
translations.idiomatic: Songgotu joined Grand Secretaries Batai, Du Lede, and others in impeaching him, and Cilv was dismissed and sent home.

sentences.zh: 十八年，京察，侍講學士顧八代隨徵稱職，翰林院以「政勤才長」注考，索額圖改注「浮躁」，竟坐降調。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year, at the metropolitan evaluation, Reader-in-Waiting Gu Badge was rated competent on campaign; the Hanlin Academy noted him as "diligent in governance and long in talent," but Songgotu changed the note to "frivolous and impetuous," and Badge was in the end demoted and transferred.
translations.idiomatic: At the Kangxi 18 metropolitan evaluation, Reader-in-Waiting Gu Badge was judged competent on campaign; the Hanlin Academy rated him "diligent in office and gifted," but Songgotu changed the appraisal to "rash and unstable," and Badge was demoted and transferred.

sentences.zh: 語詳顧八代傳。

translations.literal: The account is given in detail in the biography of Gu Badge.
translations.idiomatic: The full account appears in Gu Badge's biography.

sentences.zh: 索額圖權勢日盛。

translations.literal: Songgotu's power and influence grew daily.
translations.idiomatic: Songgotu's power grew day by day.

sentences.zh: 會地震，左都御史魏象樞入對，陳索額圖怙權貪縱狀，請嚴譴。

translations.literal: When an earthquake occurred, Left Censor-in-Chief Wei Xiangshu came to audience and set forth Songgotu's abuses of power, greed, and indulgence, requesting severe punishment.
translations.idiomatic: During an earthquake, Left Censor-in-Chief Wei Xiangshu came before the throne and detailed Songgotu's monopoly of power, greed, and excess, urging stern punishment.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「修省當自朕始！

translations.literal: The Emperor said, "Self-cultivation must begin with me!"
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said, "Reform must begin with me!"

sentences.zh: 」翌日，召索額圖及諸大臣諭曰：「茲遘地震，朕反躬修省。

translations.literal: The next day he summoned Songgotu and the other ministers and instructed them: "Now that an earthquake has occurred, I am examining myself in reflection.
translations.idiomatic: The next day he summoned Songgotu and the other ministers and said, "Heaven has sent an earthquake, and I am looking inward to amend my ways.

sentences.zh: 爾等亦宜洗滌肺腸，公忠自矢。

translations.literal: You too ought to cleanse your hearts and minds and devote yourselves to public loyalty.
translations.idiomatic: You must likewise purge your hearts and bind yourselves to public duty and loyalty.

sentences.zh: 自任用後，諸臣家計頗皆饒裕，乃朋比徇私，益加貪黷。

translations.literal: Since you have been in office, the household circumstances of many officials have grown quite prosperous, yet you form factions and show partiality, becoming ever more corrupt.
translations.idiomatic: Since I put you in office, many of you have grown quite wealthy at home, yet you band together for private ends and grow ever more corrupt.

sentences.zh: 若事情發覺，國法具在，決不爾貸！

translations.literal: If matters come to light, the laws of the state stand ready—I shall by no means spare you!"
translations.idiomatic: If your wrongdoing is exposed, the law stands ready, and I will show you no mercy!"

sentences.zh: 」是時索額圖、明珠同柄朝政，互植私黨，貪侈傾朝右，故諭及之。

translations.literal: At that time Songgotu and Mingzhu jointly wielded court policy, each planted private factions, and their greed and extravagance dominated the right flank of the court; hence the admonition touched upon them.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Songgotu and Mingzhu shared control of the government, built rival factions, and their greed and extravagance dominated the court—hence the warning.

sentences.zh: 上並書「節制謹度」榜賜焉。

translations.literal: The Emperor also wrote the words "restraint and careful measure" on a placard and bestowed it upon them.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor also inscribed the words "restraint and moderation" on a placard and gave it to them.

sentences.zh: 十九年八月，以病乞解任，上優旨獎其「勤敏練達，用兵以來，贊畫機宜」，改命為內大臣。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the nineteenth year, on grounds of illness he requested release from office; the Emperor graciously praised his "diligence, quickness, and seasoned judgment—since the opening of hostilities, he has helped plan strategy," and transferred him to the post of Inner Minister.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of Kangxi 19 he asked to retire on grounds of illness; the Emperor praised his diligence, quick wit, and seasoned counsel in wartime planning and made him an inner minister instead.

sentences.zh: 尋授議政大臣。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he was appointed a Deliberative Minister.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon appointed a deliberative minister.

sentences.zh: 先是索額圖兄噶布拉，以冊諡孝誠仁皇后推恩所生，封一等公；

translations.literal: Earlier, Songgotu's elder brother Gabbula, by grace extended for having borne Empress Xiaochengren, had been enfeoffed as a first-rank duke;
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Songgotu's elder brother Gabbula had been enfeoffed a first-rank duke by grace extended to the Empress Xiaochengren's birth family;

sentences.zh: 弟心裕，襲索尼初封一等伯；

translations.literal: his younger brother Xinyu inherited Sonin's original first-rank baronage;
translations.idiomatic: his younger brother Xinyu inherited Sonin's original first-rank barony;

sentences.zh: 法保，襲索尼加封一等公。

translations.literal: and Fabao inherited Sonin's augmented first-rank dukedom.
translations.idiomatic: and Fabao inherited Sonin's augmented first-rank dukedom.

sentences.zh: 二十三年三月，以心裕等嬾惰驕縱，責索額圖弗能教，奪內大臣、議政大臣、太子太傅，但任佐領，並奪法保一等公。

translations.literal: In the third month of the twenty-third year, because Xinyu and the others were lazy, indulgent, arrogant, and unrestrained, Songgotu was blamed for failing to instruct them; he was stripped of his posts as Inner Minister, Deliberative Minister, and Junior Preceptor to the Crown Prince, retaining only his company command, and Fabao was also stripped of his first-rank dukedom.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of Kangxi 23, Xinyu and the others were found lazy, arrogant, and unrestrained; Songgotu was blamed for failing to discipline them, stripped of his posts as inner minister, deliberative minister, and junior preceptor to the Crown Prince, and left with only his company command, while Fabao lost his dukedom.

sentences.zh: 二十五年，授領侍衛內大臣。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fifth year, he was appointed Chief Guard of the Inner Court.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 25 he was made chief guard of the inner court.

sentences.zh: 時俄羅斯屢侵黑龍江邊境，據雅克薩，其眾去復來，上發兵圍之。

translations.literal: At that time Russia repeatedly encroached upon the Heilongjiang frontier and occupied Albazin; its people withdrew and returned again, and the Emperor sent troops to besiege them.
translations.idiomatic: Russia had repeatedly raided the Heilongjiang frontier and held Albazin; though its garrison withdrew, it returned, and the Emperor sent troops to besiege the place.

sentences.zh: 察罕汗謝罪，使費耀多囉等來議界。

translations.literal: The Tsar expressed regret and sent Feiyaoduluo and others to negotiate the boundary.
translations.idiomatic: The Tsar apologized and dispatched Feiyaoduluo and others to discuss the border.

sentences.zh: 二十八年，上命索額圖與都統佟國綱往議。

translations.literal: In the twenty-eighth year, the Emperor ordered Songgotu and Commander-in-Chief Tong Guogang to go and negotiate.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 28 the Emperor ordered Songgotu and Commander-in-Chief Tong Guogang to go and negotiate.

sentences.zh: 索額圖奏謂：「尼布楚、雅克薩兩地當歸我。

translations.literal: Songgotu memorialized, saying, "Nerchinsk and Albazin should both be returned to us."
translations.idiomatic: Songgotu memorialized that Nerchinsk and Albazin ought both to be restored to the Qing.

sentences.zh: 」上曰：「尼布楚歸我，則俄羅斯貿易無所棲止，可以額爾固納河為界。

translations.literal: The Emperor said, "If Nerchinsk is returned to us, Russia will have nowhere to anchor its trade; the Argun River may serve as the boundary."
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor replied, "If we keep Nerchinsk, Russia will have nowhere to base its trade; let the Argun River be the border."

sentences.zh: 」索額圖等與議，費耀多囉果執尼布楚、雅克薩為請。

translations.literal: Songgotu and the others negotiated, and Feiyaoduluo indeed pressed for Nerchinsk and Albazin.
translations.idiomatic: In the talks Feiyaoduluo insisted on keeping Nerchinsk and Albazin.

sentences.zh: 索額圖等力斥之，仍宣上意，以額爾固納河及格爾必齊河為界，立碑而還。

translations.literal: Songgotu and the others forcefully rejected this, still proclaimed the Emperor's intent, fixed the boundary at the Argun River and the Gorbi River, erected a stele, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Songgotu and his party firmly rejected those claims, upheld the Emperor's terms, set the border at the Argun and Gorbi rivers, erected a boundary stele, and returned.

sentences.zh: 二十九年，上以裕親王福全為大將軍，擊噶爾丹，命索額圖將盛京、吉林、科爾沁兵會於巴林，敗噶爾丹於烏闌布通。

translations.literal: In the twenty-ninth year, the Emperor appointed Prince Yu Fuquan as commander-in-chief to attack Galdan, and ordered Songgotu to lead troops from Fengtian, Jilin, and the Khorchin to assemble at Bairin; Galdan was defeated at Ulan Butong.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 29 the Emperor made Prince Yu Fuquan commander-in-chief against Galdan and ordered Songgotu to concentrate Fengtian, Jilin, and Khorchin forces at Bairin; Galdan was defeated at Ulan Butong.

sentences.zh: 以不窮追，鐫四級。

translations.literal: Because he did not pursue to the end, he was stripped of four ranks.
translations.idiomatic: For failing to pursue the enemy to the end, he was demoted four ranks.

sentences.zh: 三十五年，從上親征，率八旗前鋒、察哈爾四旗及漢軍綠旗兵前行，並命督火器營。

translations.literal: In the thirty-fifth year, he accompanied the Emperor on a personal campaign, leading the vanguard of the Eight Banners, the four Chahar banners, and the Chinese Banner and Green Standard forces on the advance, and was also ordered to supervise the Firearms Brigade.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 35 he joined the Emperor's personal campaign, commanding the Eight Banners vanguard, the four Chahar banners, and the Chinese Banner and Green Standard advance forces, and was also put in charge of the Firearms Brigade.

sentences.zh: 大將軍費揚古自西路抵圖拉。

translations.literal: Commander-in-Chief Feiyanggu arrived at Tula from the western route.
translations.idiomatic: Commander-in-Chief Feiyanggu reached Tula by the western route.

sentences.zh: 上駐克魯倫河，噶爾丹遁走。

translations.literal: The Emperor halted at the Kerulen River, and Galdan fled.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor encamped on the Kerulen River while Galdan fled.

sentences.zh: 費揚古截擊之於昭莫多，大敗其眾。

translations.literal: Feiyanggu intercepted him at Jao Modo and routed his forces.
translations.idiomatic: Feiyanggu cut him off at Jao Modo and crushed his army.

sentences.zh: 三十六年，上還幸寧夏，命索額圖督水驛，會噶爾丹死。

translations.literal: In the thirty-sixth year, when the Emperor returned and visited Ningxia, he ordered Songgotu to supervise the river courier stations, and Galdan's death coincided with this.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 36, as the Emperor returned by way of Ningxia, he put Songgotu in charge of the river courier stations; Galdan died about this time.

sentences.zh: 敘功，复前所鐫級。

translations.literal: When merits were assessed, the ranks previously stripped from him were restored.
translations.idiomatic: When rewards were reckoned, his earlier demotion was reversed.

sentences.zh: 四十年九月，以老乞休，心裕代為領侍衛內大臣。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the fortieth year, on grounds of old age he requested retirement; Xinyu replaced him as Chief Guard of the Inner Court.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of Kangxi 40 he retired on account of age, and Xinyu succeeded him as chief guard of the inner court.

sentences.zh: 索額圖事皇太子謹，皇太子漸失上意。

translations.literal: Songgotu served the Crown Prince with care, but the Crown Prince gradually lost the Emperor's favor.
translations.idiomatic: Songgotu attended the Crown Prince faithfully, yet the Crown Prince was gradually falling from the Emperor's favor.

sentences.zh: 四十一年，上閱河至德州，皇太子有疾，召索額圖自京師至德州侍疾。

translations.literal: In the forty-first year, when the Emperor inspected the waterways and reached Dezhou, the Crown Prince fell ill; Songgotu was summoned from the capital to Dezhou to attend him in his illness.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 41, while the Emperor was inspecting the waterways at Dezhou, the Crown Prince fell ill and Songgotu was summoned from the capital to nurse him there.

sentences.zh: 居月馀，皇太子疾愈，還京師。

translations.literal: After more than a month, the Crown Prince recovered and returned to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: After a month and more the Crown Prince recovered and returned to Beijing.

sentences.zh: 是歲，心裕以虐斃家人奪官。

translations.literal: That year, Xinyu was stripped of office for beating a household member to death.
translations.idiomatic: That same year Xinyu was dismissed for beating a servant to death.

sentences.zh: 四十二年五月，上命執索額圖，交宗人府拘禁，諭曰：「爾為大學士，以貪惡革退，後復起用，罔知愧悔。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the forty-second year, the Emperor ordered Songgotu seized and confined in the Imperial Clan Court, instructing him: "You were a Grand Secretary, dismissed for greed and wickedness, then raised again to office, yet you know no shame or repentance.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of Kangxi 42 the Emperor had Songgotu arrested and confined in the Imperial Clan Court, saying, "You were a grand secretary, removed for greed and corruption, then restored to office without shame or repentance.

sentences.zh: 爾家人訐爾，留內三年，朕意欲寬爾。

translations.literal: Your household members denounced you; I kept you within the palace for three years, intending to treat you leniently.
translations.idiomatic: Your own household denounced you; I kept you at court three years, meaning to show you leniency.

sentences.zh: 爾乃怙過不悛，結黨妄行，議論國事。

translations.literal: Yet you clung to your faults without reform, formed factions and acted recklessly, and discussed affairs of state.
translations.idiomatic: Yet you persisted in your faults, formed factions, acted recklessly, and meddled in state affairs.

sentences.zh: 皇太子在德州，爾乘馬至中門始下，即此爾已應死。

translations.literal: When the Crown Prince was at Dezhou, you rode your horse up to the middle gate before dismounting—for this alone you deserved death.
translations.idiomatic: When the Crown Prince was at Dezhou, you rode all the way to the middle gate before dismounting—for that alone you deserved death.

sentences.zh: 爾所行事，任舉一端，無不當誅。

translations.literal: In any one thing you did, there was nothing that did not merit execution.
translations.idiomatic: Take any single thing you did—none of it fell short of a capital offense.

sentences.zh: ​​朕念爾原系大臣，心有不忍，姑貸爾死。

translations.literal: Considering that you were formerly a high minister, my heart could not bear it; for the moment I spare your life."
translations.idiomatic: Remembering that you were once a senior minister, I cannot bring myself to kill you—for now I spare your life."

sentences.zh: 」又命執索額圖諸子交心裕、法保拘禁，諭：「若別生事端，心裕、法保當族誅！

translations.literal: He also ordered Songgotu's sons seized and handed over to Xinyu and Fabao for confinement, instructing them: "If any further trouble arises, Xinyu and Fabao shall be executed with their entire clans!"
translations.idiomatic: He also had Songgotu's sons arrested and placed in the custody of Xinyu and Fabao, warning, "If any further trouble arises, Xinyu and Fabao and their entire clans shall be put to death!"

sentences.zh: 」諸臣黨附索額圖者，麻爾圖、額庫禮、溫代、邵甘、佟寶並命嚴錮，阿米達以老貸之。

translations.literal: Officials who had attached themselves to Songgotu's faction—Ma'ertu, Ekuli, Wendai, Shao Gan, Tong Bao—were all ordered strictly confined; Amida was spared on account of his age.
translations.idiomatic: Ministers who had sided with Songgotu—Ma'ertu, Ekuli, Wendai, Shao Gan, and Tong Bao—were all placed under strict confinement; Amida was spared because of his age.

sentences.zh: 又命諸臣同祖子孫在部院者，皆奪官。

translations.literal: The Emperor also ordered that all descendants of the same ancestral line serving in ministries and boards be stripped of office.
translations.idiomatic: He also stripped every descendant of Songgotu's line who held office in the ministries and boards.

sentences.zh: 江潢以家有索額圖私書，下刑部論死。

translations.literal: Jiang Huang, because he possessed a private letter from Songgotu, was sent to the Board of Punishments and sentenced to death.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Huang was sentenced to death by the Board of Punishments for keeping a private letter from Songgotu.

sentences.zh: 仍諭滿洲人與偶有來往者，漢官與交結者，皆貸不問。

translations.literal: Yet the Emperor still instructed that Manchus who had had occasional contact with him, and Chinese officials who had associated with him, were all to be pardoned and not questioned.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he also decreed that Manchus who had had casual dealings with Songgotu and Chinese officials who had consorted with him were all to be forgiven and left unprosecuted.

sentences.zh: 尋索額圖死於幽所。

translations.literal: Before long Songgotu died in confinement.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Songgotu died in custody.

sentences.zh: 後數年，皇太子以狂疾廢，上宣諭罪狀，謂：「索額圖助允礽潛謀大事，朕知其情，將索額圖處死。

translations.literal: Several years later, the Crown Prince was deposed for violent madness; the Emperor proclaimed the charges, saying, "Songgotu helped Yinreng secretly plot great matters; I knew the truth and was about to put Songgotu to death.
translations.idiomatic: Years later the Crown Prince was deposed for violent madness; proclaiming the charges, the Emperor said, "Songgotu had helped Yinreng plot treason in secret; I knew it and was ready to execute him.

sentences.zh: 今允礽欲為索額圖報仇，令朕戒慎不寧。

translations.literal: Now Yinreng seeks to avenge Songgotu, leaving me uneasy and on guard."
translations.idiomatic: Now Yinreng seeks revenge for Songgotu, and I cannot rest easy."

sentences.zh: 」並按誅索額圖二子格爾芬、阿爾吉善。

translations.literal: Songgotu's two sons, Ge'erfen and A'erjishan, were also executed accordingly.
translations.idiomatic: Songgotu's sons Ge'erfen and A'erjishan were executed as well.

sentences.zh: 他日，上謂廷臣曰：「昔索額圖懷私，倡議皇太子服禦俱用黃色，一切儀制幾與朕相似。

translations.literal: On another day the Emperor told the court ministers, "Formerly Songgotu, acting from private motive, proposed that the Crown Prince's court dress and equipage all use yellow, so that in every ritual form he nearly resembled me.
translations.idiomatic: On another occasion the Emperor told his ministers, "Songgotu once urged, out of private interest, that the Crown Prince's dress and regalia all be yellow, so that in ritual he nearly matched me.

sentences.zh: 驕縱之漸，實由於此。

translations.literal: The gradual rise of arrogance and indulgence in fact stemmed from this.
translations.idiomatic: The Crown Prince's slide into arrogance began there.

sentences.zh: 索額圖誠本朝第一罪人也！

translations.literal: Songgotu was truly this dynasty's foremost criminal!"
translations.idiomatic: Songgotu was the greatest criminal of this dynasty!"

translations.literal: " (closing quotation mark in the source.)
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor concluded.

sentences.zh: 明珠，字端範，納喇氏，滿洲正黃旗人，葉赫貝勒金台石孫。

translations.literal: Mingzhu, styled Duanfan, of the Nara clan, was a man of the Manchu Plain Yellow Banner and the grandson of Yehe beile Gintaisi.
translations.idiomatic: Mingzhu, style name Duanfan, of the Nara clan and the Plain Yellow Banner, was the grandson of Yehe beile Gintaisi.

sentences.zh: 父尼雅哈，當太祖滅葉赫，來降，授佐領。

translations.literal: His father Niyaha, when the Taizu destroyed Yehe, came over in surrender and was appointed a company commander.
translations.idiomatic: His father Niyaha submitted when the Taizu conquered Yehe and was made a company commander.

sentences.zh: 明珠自侍衛授鑾儀衛治儀正，遷內務府郎中。

translations.literal: Mingzhu, from guardsman, was appointed Director of Ceremonies in the Imperial Procession Guard, then promoted to Director in the Imperial Household Department.
translations.idiomatic: Mingzhu rose from guardsman to director of ceremonies in the Imperial Procession Guard, then to director in the Imperial Household Department.

sentences.zh: 康熙三年，擢總管。

translations.literal: In the third year of Kangxi, he was promoted to superintendent.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 3 he was promoted superintendent.

sentences.zh: 五年，授弘文院學士。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, he was appointed Academician of the Hall of Literary Glory.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 5 he became an academician of the Hall of Literary Glory.

sentences.zh: 七年，命閱淮、揚河工，議復興化白駒場舊閘，鑿黃河北岸引河。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, he was ordered to inspect the Huai and Yang river works, and proposed restoring the old sluice at Xinghua's Baijuchang and cutting a diversion canal on the north bank of the Yellow River.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 7 he was sent to inspect the Huai-Yang river works and proposed restoring the old sluice at Xinghua's Baijuchang and opening a diversion on the Yellow River's north bank.

sentences.zh: 旋授刑部尚書。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he was appointed Minister of the Board of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made minister of the Board of Punishments.

sentences.zh: 改都察院左都御史，充經筵講官。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Left Censor-in-Chief of the Censorate and appointed lecturer at the Classics Colloquium.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to left censor-in-chief of the Censorate and made a lecturer at the Classics Colloquium.

sentences.zh: 十一年，遷兵部尚書。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year, he was promoted to Minister of the Board of War.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 11 he became minister of the Board of War.

sentences.zh: 十二年，上幸南苑，閱八旗甲兵於晾鷹台。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year, when the Emperor visited the Southern Park, he reviewed the armor and troops of the Eight Banners at the Hawk-Drying Terrace.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 12, when the Emperor visited the Southern Park, the Eight Banners reviewed their arms and armor at the Hawk-Drying Terrace.

sentences.zh: 明珠先布條教使練習之，及期，軍容整肅，上嘉其能，因著為令。

translations.literal: Mingzhu first issued detailed regulations for their practice; when the day came, the army's bearing was orderly and stern, and the Emperor praised his ability and had the rules established as an edict.
translations.idiomatic: Mingzhu first laid down drill regulations; when the day came the troops were trim and disciplined, the Emperor praised his competence, and the rules were promulgated as standing orders.

sentences.zh: 康熙初，南疆大定，留重兵鎮之：吳三桂雲南，尚可喜廣東，耿精忠福建。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Kangxi, the south was largely pacified, and heavy troops were left to garrison it: Wu Sangui in Yunnan, Shang Kexi in Guangdong, and Geng Jingzhong in Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Kangxi, with the south largely pacified, heavy garrisons remained: Wu Sangui in Yunnan, Shang Kexi in Guangdong, and Geng Jingzhong in Fujian.

sentences.zh: 十馀年，漸跋扈，三桂尤驕縱。

translations.literal: After more than ten years they gradually became overbearing and insubordinate, and Wu Sangui was especially arrogant and unrestrained.
translations.idiomatic: After a decade they grew increasingly overbearing, Wu Sangui most of all.

sentences.zh: 可喜亦憂之，疏請撤籓，歸老海城。

translations.literal: Shang Kexi also grew anxious and memorialized requesting withdrawal of the princely fief and retirement to his old home at Haicheng.
translations.idiomatic: Shang Kexi too grew uneasy and asked to surrender his fief and retire to Haicheng.

sentences.zh: 精忠、三桂繼請。

translations.literal: Jingzhong and Wu Sangui followed with similar requests.
translations.idiomatic: Geng Jingzhong and Wu Sangui soon did the same.

sentences.zh: 上召諸大臣詢方略，戶部尚書米思翰、刑部尚書莫洛等主撤，明珠和之。

translations.literal: The Emperor summoned the ministers to inquire their strategy; Minister of Revenue Misihan, Minister of Punishments Moluo, and others advocated withdrawal, and Mingzhu agreed with them.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor summoned his ministers for counsel; Minister of Revenue Misihan, Minister of Punishments Moluo, and others favored withdrawal, and Mingzhu agreed.

sentences.zh: 諸大臣皆默然。

translations.literal: The other ministers all remained silent.
translations.idiomatic: The rest of the ministers said nothing.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「三桂等蓄謀久，不早除之，將養癰成患。

translations.literal: The Emperor said, "Wu Sangui and the others have long nursed their designs; if they are not removed early, the sore will be nurtured into a grave illness.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said, "Wu Sangui and the others have plotted for years; if we do not remove them soon, we will nurse a boil into a plague.

sentences.zh: 今日撤亦反，不撤亦反，不若先發。

translations.literal: Today they will rebel whether we withdraw or not; better to strike first."
translations.idiomatic: They will rebel whether we withdraw the fiefs or not—better to move first."

sentences.zh: 」因下詔許之。

translations.literal: Accordingly an edict was issued granting permission.
translations.idiomatic: An edict was then issued approving the withdrawal.

sentences.zh: 三桂遂反，精忠及可喜子之信皆叛應之。

translations.literal: Wu Sangui thereupon rebelled, and Jingzhong and Shang Kexi's son Zhixin all rose in revolt in response.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Sangui rebelled at once, and Geng Jingzhong and Shang Kexi's son Zhixin rose in support.

sentences.zh: 時爭咎建議者，索額圖請誅之。

translations.literal: At the time many blamed those who had proposed the policy; Songgotu requested that they be put to death.
translations.idiomatic: When blame fell on those who had urged withdrawal, Songgotu called for their execution.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「此出自朕意，他人何罪？

translations.literal: The Emperor said, "This came from my own intent—what crime do others have?"
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor replied, "This was my decision—what fault is there in others?"

sentences.zh: 」明珠由是稱上旨。

translations.literal: From this Mingzhu was regarded as having accorded with the Emperor's intent.
translations.idiomatic: From then on Mingzhu was seen as having spoken with the Emperor's mind.

sentences.zh: 十四年，調吏部尚書。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year, he was transferred to Minister of the Board of Civil Appointments.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 14 he was transferred to minister of the Board of Civil Appointments.

sentences.zh: 十六年，授武英殿大學士，屢充實錄、方略、一統志、明史諸書總裁，累加太子太師。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year, he was appointed Grand Secretary of the Hall of Military Glory, repeatedly served as chief compiler of the Veritable Records, military chronicles, unified gazetteer, and History of Ming, and was repeatedly given the additional title of Junior Preceptor to the Crown Prince.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 16 he became grand secretary of the Hall of Military Glory, repeatedly headed compilations of the Veritable Records, military chronicles, unified gazetteer, and History of Ming, and accumulated additional honors as junior preceptor to the Crown Prince.

sentences.zh: 迨三叛既平，上諭廷臣以前議撤籓，惟明珠等能稱旨，且曰：「當時有請誅建議者，朕若從之，皆含冤泉壤矣！

translations.literal: After the three rebellions were pacified, the Emperor told the court ministers that in the earlier deliberation on withdrawing the fiefs, only Mingzhu and others had accorded with his intent, and said, "At the time there were those who asked that the proposers be put to death; had I followed them, those men would now lie wrongfully in their graves!"
translations.idiomatic: After the three rebellions were crushed, the Emperor told his ministers that in the debate over withdrawing the fiefs only Mingzhu and a few others had matched his intent, adding, "Some then demanded the deaths of those who had urged withdrawal; had I listened, innocent men would now lie dead underground!"

translations.literal: " (closing quotation mark in the source.)
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor concluded.

sentences.zh: 明珠既擅政，簠簋不飭，貨賄山積。

translations.literal: Once Mingzhu monopolized government, his conduct was unrestrained and bribes piled up like mountains.
translations.idiomatic: Once Mingzhu dominated the government, he abandoned proper restraint and bribes heaped up like mountains.

sentences.zh: 佛倫、餘國柱其黨也，援引致高位。

translations.literal: Folun and Yuguo were his partisans; he recommended them and brought them to high position.
translations.idiomatic: Folun and Yuguo were his men; he promoted them to high office.

sentences.zh: 靳輔督南河，主築堤束水，下游不濬自通。

translations.literal: Jin Fu, supervising the Southern Rivers, advocated building dikes to confine the water so that the lower reaches would clear without dredging.
translations.idiomatic: Jin Fu, as supervisor of the Southern Rivers, argued for building dikes to confine the current so the lower course would clear itself without dredging.

sentences.zh: 於成龍等議濬下游，與異議。

translations.literal: Yu Chenglong and others advocated dredging the lower reaches and differed in opinion.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Chenglong and others favored dredging the lower reaches and disagreed.

sentences.zh: 輔興屯田，議者謂不便於民，多不右輔，明珠獨是其議。

translations.literal: In assisting the farming colonies, critics said they were inconvenient for the people; most did not support Jin Fu, but Mingzhu alone endorsed his proposal.
translations.idiomatic: On the farming colonies Jin Fu had proposed, critics said they burdened the people; most sided against him, but Mingzhu alone supported his plan.

sentences.zh: 蔡毓榮、張汧皆明珠所薦引者也，迨得罪按治，恐累舉者，傅輕比，上諭斥，始定。

translations.literal: Cai Yurong and Zhang Qian were both men Mingzhu had recommended; when they were found guilty and prosecuted, fearing that the recommender would be implicated, lighter penalties were proposed, but the Emperor rebuked this and the matter was settled.
translations.idiomatic: Cai Yurong and Zhang Qian had both been promoted by Mingzhu; when they were prosecuted for offenses, lighter sentences were proposed lest their patron be implicated, but the Emperor rebuked the move and the cases were settled.

sentences.zh: 與索額圖互植黨相傾軋。

translations.literal: He and Songgotu each planted factions and strove to overthrow the other.
translations.idiomatic: He and Songgotu built rival factions and worked to ruin each other.

sentences.zh: 索額圖生而貴盛，性倨肆，有不附己者顯斥之，於朝士獨親李光地。

translations.literal: Songgotu was born to wealth and eminence, and by nature was arrogant and overbearing; those who would not attach themselves to him he openly drove away, and among court officials he was intimate only with Li Guangdi.
translations.idiomatic: Born to wealth and rank, Songgotu was arrogant by nature; he openly ostracized anyone who would not follow him and kept close only to Li Guangdi among the court officials.

sentences.zh: 明珠則務謙和，輕財好施，以招來新進，異己者以陰謀陷之，與徐乾學等相結。

translations.literal: Mingzhu, by contrast, cultivated humility and harmony, was light with wealth and generous in giving, to win over newcomers; those who differed from him he ruined by secret plots, and he allied himself with Xu Qianxue and others.
translations.idiomatic: Mingzhu, by contrast, affected humility, spent freely to win over newcomers, and used covert schemes against opponents while allying with Xu Qianxue and his circle.

sentences.zh: 索額圖善事皇太子，而明珠反之，朝士有侍皇太子者，皆陰斥去。

translations.literal: Songgotu was skilled at serving the Crown Prince, while Mingzhu took the opposite course; court officials who attended the Crown Prince were all secretly driven away.
translations.idiomatic: Songgotu cultivated the Crown Prince, whereas Mingzhu undermined him; officials who sided with the heir were quietly removed.

sentences.zh: 薦湯斌傅皇太子，即以傾斌。

translations.literal: He recommended Tang Bin to tutor the Crown Prince, then used this very fact to bring Bin down.
translations.idiomatic: He had Tang Bin appointed tutor to the Crown Prince, then turned that very appointment against him.

sentences.zh: 會天久不雨，光地所薦講官德格勒明易，上命筮，得夬，因陳小人居鼎鉉，天屯其膏，語斥明珠。

translations.literal: When heaven long withheld rain, the lecturer Degeli, whom Guangdi had recommended and who was versed in the Changes, was ordered to divine; the hexagram Guai was obtained, and he thereupon stated that petty men occupied the tripod cauldron, that heaven hoarded its bounty, and in his words rebuked Mingzhu.
translations.idiomatic: During a prolonged drought the Emperor had Degeli, a lecturer on the Changes whom Guangdi had recommended, cast the oracle; the hexagram Guai appeared, and Degeli declared that petty men held power while heaven withheld its bounty—words aimed at Mingzhu.

sentences.zh: 事具德格勒傳。

translations.literal: The matter is given in full in the biography of Degeli.
translations.idiomatic: The full account appears in Degeli's biography.

sentences.zh: 二十七年，御史郭琇疏劾：「明珠、國柱背公營私，閣中票擬皆出明珠指麾，輕重任意。

translations.literal: In the twenty-seventh year, Censor Guo Xiu submitted a memorial of impeachment: "Mingzhu and Guozhu betray the public for private gain; all draft approvals in the Grand Secretariat issue from Mingzhu's direction, and weight and lightness are at his arbitrary will.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 27 Censor Guo Xiu memorialized: "Mingzhu and Yuguo betray the public for private gain; every draft approval in the Grand Secretariat follows Mingzhu's orders, and he decides what matters and what does not.

sentences.zh: 國柱承其風旨，即有舛錯，同官莫敢駁正。

translations.literal: Guozhu follows his tone and intent; even when there are errors, fellow officials dare not correct them.
translations.idiomatic: Yuguo echoes his wishes; even when errors appear, colleagues dare not correct them.

sentences.zh: 聖明時有詰責，漫無省改。

translations.literal: Though the sage Emperor from time to time rebukes them, they show no reflection or reform.
translations.idiomatic: Though Your Majesty rebukes them from time to time, they show no remorse or reform.

sentences.zh: 凡奉諭旨或稱善，明珠則曰'由我力荐'；

translations.literal: Whenever an imperial edict is received and something is praised, Mingzhu says, 'That was through my strong recommendation';
translations.idiomatic: When an edict arrives and something is praised, Mingzhu says, 'That was my recommendation';

sentences.zh: 或稱不善，明珠則曰'上意不喜，我從容挽救'；

translations.literal: or when something is disapproved, Mingzhu says, 'The Emperor's mind is displeased; I have calmly rescued the matter';
translations.idiomatic: when something is criticized, he says, 'His Majesty was displeased, but I smoothed it over';

sentences.zh: 且任意附益，市恩立威，因而要結群心，挾取貨賄。

translations.literal: and he arbitrarily adds embellishments, trades favors to build prestige, and thereby binds men's hearts and extorts bribes.
translations.idiomatic: he embellishes at will, trades favors for authority, binds men's loyalty, and extorts bribes.

sentences.zh: 日奏事畢，出中左門，滿、漢部院諸臣拱立以待，密語移時，上意罔不宣露。

translations.literal: Each day when audience is finished, he exits the central left gate; Manchu and Chinese officials of the ministries and boards stand bowed in waiting; he whispers for a long time, and nothing of the Emperor's intent fails to be disclosed.
translations.idiomatic: After daily audience he leaves by the central left gate while Manchu and Chinese ministers wait bowing; he whispers with them at length, and the Emperor's intentions are always leaked.

sentences.zh: 部院事稍有關係者，必請命而行。

translations.literal: Whenever a matter in a ministry or board has the slightest connection, he must request orders before acting.
translations.idiomatic: Even minor business in the ministries must await his orders before proceeding.

sentences.zh: 明珠廣結黨羽，滿洲則佛倫、格斯特及其族侄富拉塔、錫珠等，凡會議會推，力為把持；

translations.literal: Mingzhu widely knotted factions: among Manchus, Folun, Gest, and their clansmen Fulate and Xizhu, and at every joint conference or joint recommendation he strove to control outcomes;
translations.idiomatic: Mingzhu built a wide faction: among Manchus, Folun, Gest, and their kinsmen Fulate and Xizhu controlled every conference and recommendation;

sentences.zh: 漢人則國柱為之囊橐，督撫籓臬員缺，國柱等展轉徵賄，必滿欲而後止。

translations.literal: among Chinese, Guozhu served as his purse; for governorships, provincial posts, and circuit intendant vacancies, Guozhu and others passed bribes through intermediaries and would not stop until their desires were fully satisfied.
translations.idiomatic: among Chinese officials Yuguo was his purse; governorships and provincial posts were sold through him until every demand was met.

sentences.zh: 康熙二十三年學道報滿應升者，率往論價，缺皆預定。

translations.literal: Those who had completed their term as educational commissioners in Kangxi 23 and were due for promotion were generally made to bargain over price, and vacancies were all fixed in advance.
translations.idiomatic: Educational commissioners due for promotion in Kangxi 23 were routinely asked to bid for posts, and vacancies were fixed in advance.

sentences.zh: 靳輔與明珠交結，初議開下河，以為當任輔，欣然欲行。

translations.literal: Jin Fu was allied with Mingzhu; when the opening of the lower river was first discussed, it was thought that Fu should be entrusted with it, and he was eager to undertake it.
translations.idiomatic: Jin Fu was allied with Mingzhu; when opening the lower river was first proposed, Fu was expected to lead the work and was eager to do so.

sentences.zh: 及上欲別任，則以於成龍方沐上眷，舉以應命，而成龍官止按察使，題奏權仍屬輔，此時未有阻撓意也。

translations.literal: When the Emperor wished to appoint another, they nominated Yu Chenglong, who was then enjoying imperial favor, to answer the order; yet Chenglong's rank was only surveillance commissioner, and the power of memorial submission still belonged to Fu—at that time there was still no intent to obstruct.
translations.idiomatic: When the Emperor wanted someone else, they nominated the favored Yu Chenglong, though he was only a surveillance commissioner and memorial authority still rested with Fu—at that point they had not yet meant to obstruct.

sentences.zh: 及輔張大其事，與成龍議不合，乃始一力阻撓。

translations.literal: When Fu magnified the affair and his views clashed with Chenglong's, only then did he begin to obstruct with all his strength.
translations.idiomatic: Only when Fu escalated the project and clashed with Chenglong did he begin to obstruct it outright.

sentences.zh: 明珠自知罪戾，對人柔顏甘語，百計款曲，而陰行鷙害，意毒謀險。

translations.literal: Mingzhu, knowing his own guilt, showed others a gentle face and sweet words, using a hundred devices of courtesy, yet secretly practiced fierce harm—his intent was poisonous and his schemes treacherous.
translations.idiomatic: Aware of his guilt, Mingzhu spoke softly in public while secretly doing fierce harm—his designs were poisonous and treacherous.

sentences.zh: 最忌者言官，惟恐發其奸狀，考選科道，輒與訂約，章奏必使先聞。

translations.literal: What he most feared were censorial officials, dreading lest his wicked conduct be exposed; in selecting and examining censors, he would make agreements with them, and memorials had to be shown to him first.
translations.idiomatic: He feared censors most of all and made candidates for censorial posts pledge to show him memorials before submission.

sentences.zh: 當佛倫為左都御史，見御史李興謙屢疏稱旨，吳震方頗有彈劾，即令借事排陷。

translations.literal: When Folun was Left Censor-in-Chief, seeing that Censor Li Xingqian's repeated memorials pleased the Emperor and that Wu Zhenfang was inclined to impeach, he ordered that they be framed on pretexts.
translations.idiomatic: When Folun was left censor-in-chief, he had Li Xingqian framed after Li's memorials won praise, and likewise targeted the impeaching Wu Zhenfang.

sentences.zh: 明珠智術足以彌縫罪惡，又有國柱奸謀附和，負恩亂政。

translations.literal: Mingzhu's craft was sufficient to cover over crimes, and with Guozhu's wicked schemes in support, he was ungrateful and disturbed government.
translations.idiomatic: Mingzhu's cunning covered his crimes, Yuguo's schemes backed him, and together they were ungrateful disturbers of government.

sentences.zh: 伏冀立加嚴譴。

translations.literal: I humbly pray that stern punishment be immediately imposed."
translations.idiomatic: I beg that stern punishment be imposed at once."

translations.literal: " (closing quotation mark in the source.)
translations.idiomatic: The memorial concluded.

sentences.zh: 疏入，上諭吏部曰：「國家建官分職，必矢志精白，大法小廉。

translations.literal: When the memorial entered, the Emperor instructed the Board of Civil Appointments: "In establishing offices and dividing duties, the state requires men of steadfast integrity and great law with small self-interest.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial arrived, the Emperor told the Board of Civil Appointments, "In appointing officials the state demands steadfast integrity and scrupulous conduct.

sentences.zh: 今在廷諸臣，自大學士以下，惟知互相結引，徇私傾陷。

translations.literal: Now the officials at court, from Grand Secretaries downward, know only how to band together for mutual support and show partiality in overthrowing others.
translations.idiomatic: Yet from grand secretaries down, they know only factional alliance and private vendettas.

sentences.zh: 凡遇會議，一二倡率於前，眾附和於後，一意詭隨。

translations.literal: Whenever a conference is held, one or two lead the way in front and the multitude echo behind, all following one bent of perverse compliance.
translations.idiomatic: At every conference one or two lead and the rest follow, all bending to faction.

sentences.zh: 廷議如此，國是何憑？

translations.literal: When court deliberation is like this, upon what can the state rely?
translations.idiomatic: When deliberation runs thus, what foundation has the state?

sentences.zh: 至於緊要員缺，特令會同推舉，原期得人，亦欲令被舉者警心滌慮，恐致累及舉者，而貪黷匪類，往往敗露。

translations.literal: As for important vacancies, the court specially orders joint recommendation, originally expecting to obtain the right men and also wishing those recommended to guard their hearts and cleanse their thoughts, fearing lest the recommender be implicated; yet greedy and corrupt sorts are often exposed.
translations.idiomatic: Important posts are filled by joint recommendation, meant to yield worthy men and to make nominees watch their conduct lest their patrons be implicated—yet the corrupt are constantly exposed.

sentences.zh: 此皆植黨納賄所致。

translations.literal: All this stems from planting factions and accepting bribes.
translations.idiomatic: All this comes of factions and bribery.

sentences.zh: 朕不忍加罪大臣，且用兵時有曾著勞績者，免其發覺。

translations.literal: I cannot bear to punish great ministers, and moreover among them are some who rendered merit in time of war; let their exposure be spared.
translations.idiomatic: I will not punish senior ministers outright, especially those who served well in war; let their crimes pass unexposed.

sentences.zh: 罷明珠大學士，交領侍衛內大臣酌用。

translations.literal: Remove Mingzhu from the Grand Secretaryship and hand him over to the Chief Guard of the Inner Court for appropriate use."
translations.idiomatic: Dismiss Mingzhu from the grand secretaryship and assign him to the chief guard of the inner court."

sentences.zh: 」未幾，授內大臣。

translations.literal: Before long he was appointed Inner Minister.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was made an inner minister.

sentences.zh: 後從上徵噶爾丹，督西路軍餉，敘功復原級。

translations.literal: Later he followed the Emperor in the campaign against Galdan, supervised military supplies on the western route, and when merits were assessed his former rank was restored.
translations.idiomatic: He later joined the campaign against Galdan, supervised western-route supplies, and had his former rank restored for merit.

sentences.zh: 明珠自罷政後，雖權勢未替，然為內大臣者二十年，竟不復柄用。

translations.literal: After Mingzhu left office, though his power and influence were not diminished, yet for twenty years as Inner Minister he was never again put in charge of policy.
translations.idiomatic: After leaving office Mingzhu retained influence, but for twenty years as inner minister he never again held real power.

sentences.zh: 四十七年，卒。

translations.literal: In the forty-seventh year he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Kangxi 47.

sentences.zh: 子性德、揆敘自有傳。

translations.literal: His sons Xingde and Kui Xu have their own biographies.
translations.idiomatic: His sons Xingde and Kui Xu have separate biographies.

sentences.zh: -{余}-國柱，字兩石，湖廣大冶人。

translations.literal: Yu {Guozhu}, styled Liangshi, was a native of Daye in Huguang.
translations.idiomatic: Yu {Guozhu}, style name Liangshi, was from Daye in Huguang.

sentences.zh: 順治九年進士，授兗州推官。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Shunzhi he passed the jinshi examination and was appointed magistrate of Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in Shunzhi 9 and was appointed magistrate of Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 遷行人司行人，轉戶部主事。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Clerk in the Bureau of Envoys, then to Director in the Board of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He became a clerk in the Bureau of Envoys, then a director in the Board of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 康熙十五年，考授戶科給事中。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year of Kangxi, by examination he was appointed Supervising Censor in the Revenue Section.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 15 he was made a supervising censor in the revenue section by examination.

sentences.zh: 時方用兵，國柱屢疏言籌餉事，語多精覈。

translations.literal: At that time war was underway; Guozhu repeatedly memorialized on raising supplies, and his words were mostly precise and exact.
translations.idiomatic: With war underway, Yuguo memorialized repeatedly on supplies in precise, well-argued terms.

sentences.zh: 二十年，擢左副都御史。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year he was promoted to Vice Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 20 he was promoted vice censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 旋授江寧巡撫，請設機制寬大緞疋。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he was appointed Governor of Jiangning and requested the establishment of looms for wide satin bolts.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made governor of Jiangning and asked to set up looms for wide satin bolts.

sentences.zh: 得旨：「非常用之物，何為勞費？

translations.literal: He received the edict: "This is not an item in regular use—why labor and spend?"
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor replied, "These are not everyday goods—why waste labor and expense?"

sentences.zh: 」當明珠用事，國柱務罔利以迎合之，及內轉左都御史，遷戶部尚書，湯斌繼國柱撫江蘇；

translations.literal: When Mingzhu was in power, Guozhu strove for illicit profit to please him; when he was transferred within the capital to Left Censor-in-Chief and promoted to Minister of Revenue, Tang Bin succeeded Guozhu as governor of Jiangsu;
translations.idiomatic: While Mingzhu held power, Yuguo sought illicit profit to please him; promoted to left censor-in-chief and minister of revenue, he was succeeded in Jiangsu by Tang Bin;

sentences.zh: 國柱索斌獻明珠金，斌不能應，由是傾之。

translations.literal: Guozhu demanded that Bin present gold to Mingzhu; Bin could not comply, and for this reason was overthrown.
translations.idiomatic: Yuguo demanded that Bin pay gold to Mingzhu; when Bin refused, Yuguo ruined him.

sentences.zh: 二十六年，授武英殿大學士，益與明珠結，一時稱為「-{余}-秦檜」。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year he was appointed Grand Secretary of the Hall of Military Glory, bound himself still closer to Mingzhu, and for a time was called "Yu {Qin Hui}."
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 26 he became grand secretary of the Hall of Military Glory, drew still closer to Mingzhu, and was nicknamed "Yu {Qin Hui}."

sentences.zh: 會上謁陵，中途召-{于}-成龍入對，成龍盡發明珠、國柱等貪私。

translations.literal: When the Emperor was visiting the imperial tombs, he summoned Yu {Chenglong} en route for audience; Chenglong fully exposed the greed and private conduct of Mingzhu, Guozhu, and others.
translations.idiomatic: During a tomb visit the Emperor summoned Yu {Chenglong} en route; Chenglong exposed the corruption of Mingzhu, Yuguo, and their circle.

sentences.zh: 上歸詢高士奇，士奇亦以狀聞。

translations.literal: On his return the Emperor questioned Gao Shiqi, and Shiqi also reported the facts.
translations.idiomatic: On returning, the Emperor questioned Gao Shiqi, who confirmed the reports.

sentences.zh: 及郭琇疏論劾，言者蜂起，國柱門人陳世安亦具疏糾之，頗中要害，國柱遂奪官。

translations.literal: When Guo Xiu's memorial of impeachment followed, accusers swarmed forth; Guozhu's disciple Chen Shi'an also submitted a memorial of correction that struck vital points, and Guozhu was stripped of office.
translations.idiomatic: After Guo Xiu's memorial, accusers multiplied; Yuguo's protégé Chen Shi'an submitted a telling impeachment, and Yuguo was dismissed.

sentences.zh: 既出都，於江寧治第宅，營生計，復為給事中何金蘭所劾，命逐之回籍。

translations.literal: After leaving the capital, he built a mansion at Jiangning and managed his livelihood; he was again impeached by Supervising Censor He Jinlan and ordered expelled back to his native place.
translations.idiomatic: After leaving Beijing he built a mansion in Jiangning and pursued profit until Supervising Censor He Jinlan impeached him and he was sent home.

sentences.zh: 卒於家。

translations.literal: He died at home.
translations.idiomatic: He died at home.

sentences.zh: 佛倫，舒穆祿氏，滿洲正白旗人。

translations.literal: Folun, of the Sumuru clan, was a man of the Manchu Plain White Banner.
translations.idiomatic: Folun of the Sumuru clan was a Manchu of the Plain White Banner.

sentences.zh: 自筆帖式累遷內閣學士。

translations.literal: From clerk of memorials he was promoted step by step to Academician of the Grand Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He rose from memorial clerk to grand secretariat academician.

sentences.zh: 吳三桂既死，其孫世璠猶據滇、黔，命佛倫總理糧餉，通鎮遠運道，旋兼理四川糧餉。

translations.literal: After Wu Sangui died, his grandson Shifan still held Yunnan and Guizhou; Folun was ordered to oversee grain supplies, open the transport route through Zhenyuan, and soon was also put in charge of Sichuan grain supplies.
translations.idiomatic: After Wu Sangui's death his grandson Shifan still held Yunnan and Guizhou; Folun oversaw grain transport, opened the Zhenyuan route, and soon took charge of Sichuan supplies as well.

sentences.zh: 事平，遷刑部侍郎。

translations.literal: When affairs were settled, he was transferred to Vice Minister of the Board of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: After the rebellion ended he became vice minister of the Board of Punishments.

sentences.zh: 尋遷左都御史，擢工部尚書，轉刑、戶兩部。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he was transferred to Left Censor-in-Chief, promoted to Minister of the Board of Works, and then transferred to the Boards of Punishments and Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made left censor-in-chief, then minister of works, and later of punishments and revenue.

sentences.zh: 先是下河工程，靳輔與按察使於成龍議不​​協，命佛倫偕侍郎熊一瀟等勘議。

translations.literal: Earlier, in the lower-river project, Jin Fu and Surveillance Commissioner Yu Chenglong could not agree; Folun was ordered to go with Vice Minister Xiong Yixiao and others to investigate and deliberate.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, on the lower-river project, Jin Fu and Surveillance Commissioner Yu Chenglong had clashed; Folun was sent with Vice Minister Xiong Yixiao and others to investigate.

sentences.zh: 佛倫受明珠指，議如輔言，為總漕慕天顏所劾。

translations.literal: Folun, acting on Mingzhu's direction, deliberated in accord with Fu's view and was impeached by Director-General of Grain Transport Mu Tianyan.
translations.idiomatic: Following Mingzhu's orders, Folun sided with Fu and was impeached by grain transport director Mu Tianyan.

sentences.zh: 御史陸祖修亦劾佛倫袒輔，且言：「九卿會議時，尚書科爾坤等阿佛倫意，尚書張玉書、左都御史徐乾學言興屯所佔民田應還之民，科爾坤置不聞。

translations.literal: Censor Lu Zuxiu also impeached Folun for favoring Fu, and stated: "At the conference of the Nine Ministers, Minister Kuo'erken and others flattered Folun's intent; Ministers Zhang Yushu and Left Censor-in-Chief Xu Qianxue said that farmland seized for state colonies should be returned to the people, but Kuo'erken paid no heed.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Lu Zuxiu also accused Folun of favoring Fu, noting that at the Nine Ministers' conference Kuo'erken flattered Folun while Zhang Yushu and Xu Qianxue argued that colony lands should be returned to the people—Kuo'erken ignored them.

sentences.zh: 他九卿或不得見隻字。

translations.literal: The other ministers sometimes could not see a single character."
translations.idiomatic: Other ministers sometimes never saw the documents at all."

sentences.zh: 」上怒，下部嚴議。

translations.literal: The Emperor was angry and sent the matter down for severe deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor was furious and ordered a severe inquiry.

sentences.zh: 及郭琇劾明珠，指佛倫為明珠黨，因解佛倫任。

translations.literal: When Guo Xiu impeached Mingzhu and identified Folun as a member of Mingzhu's faction, Folun was accordingly removed from office.
translations.idiomatic: When Guo Xiu impeached Mingzhu and named Folun as his partisan, Folun was dismissed.

sentences.zh: 召輔等廷對，佛倫乃奏停屯田，並汰前所設官。

translations.literal: Fu and others were summoned for court debate; Folun then memorialized to halt the farming colonies and also to eliminate the offices previously established.
translations.idiomatic: Jin Fu and others were summoned to debate at court; Folun then memorialized to halt the colonies and abolish the offices created for them.

sentences.zh: 部議奪佛倫官，上命留佐領。

translations.literal: The ministry deliberated stripping Folun of office; the Emperor ordered that he retain his company command.
translations.idiomatic: The ministry recommended stripping his office; the Emperor let him keep his company command.

sentences.zh: 旋授內務府總管。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he was appointed Superintendent of the Imperial Household Department.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made superintendent of the Imperial Household Department.

sentences.zh: 出為山東巡撫，疏請均賦役，令紳民一體應役，詔嘉其實心任事。

translations.literal: Sent out as Governor of Shandong, he memorialized requesting equalization of tax and corvée labor, ordering gentry and commoners alike to perform service; an edict praised his sincere devotion to duty.
translations.idiomatic: As governor of Shandong he asked that gentry and commoners alike bear corvée equally; the court praised his conscientious service.

sentences.zh: 初，濰縣知縣硃敦厚以贓私為巡撫錢鎯所發，乞徐乾學請於鎯，獲免，且內擢主事。

translations.literal: Earlier, Zhuxian County Magistrate Zhu Dunhou had been exposed for corruption by Governor Qian Heng; he begged Xu Qianxue to intercede with Heng, was spared, and was even promoted within the capital to Director.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Weixian magistrate Zhu Dunhou had been exposed for graft by Governor Qian Heng; he secured Xu Qianxue's intercession, escaped punishment, and was even promoted to director in Beijing.

sentences.zh: 至是事發，下佛倫鞫實，乾學坐奪官。

translations.literal: When the matter now broke open, the case was sent down to Folun to investigate the facts; Qianxue was stripped of office on conviction.
translations.idiomatic: When the affair surfaced, Folun investigated; Xu Qianxue lost his office.

sentences.zh: 佛倫又劾琇知吳江縣時，嘗侵公帑，其父景昌故名爾標，乃明御史黃宗昌奴，坐賊黨誅，琇改父名冒封典，當追奪。

translations.literal: Folun also impeached Xiu, saying that when he was magistrate of Wujiang County he had once embezzled public funds; his father Jingchang had originally been named Erbiao and was a bondsman of Ming censor Huang Zongchang, executed as a bandit partisan; Xiu changed his father's name to obtain posthumous honors by fraud, which ought to be revoked.
translations.idiomatic: Folun also impeached Guo Xiu for embezzling public funds as Wujiang magistrate and charged that Xiu's father Jingchang, originally the bondsman Erbiao of Ming censor Huang Zongchang, executed as a rebel, had been renamed so Xiu could claim honors by fraud—honors that should be revoked.

sentences.zh: 乾學故附明珠，後相失，或傳琇疏乾學實主之，故佛倫以是報。

translations.literal: Qianxue had formerly attached himself to Mingzhu, but later they fell out; some said that Xiu's memorial against Qianxue was in fact directed by Qianxue himself, and for this reason Folun struck back in this way.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Qianxue had once sided with Mingzhu but later broke with him; some said Guo Xiu's attack on Qianxue was really Qianxue's own doing, which Folun now repaid.

sentences.zh: 尋擢川陝總督，入為禮部尚書。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he was promoted to Governor-General of Shaanxi and Sichuan, then entered the capital as Minister of the Board of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made governor-general of Shaanxi and Sichuan, then minister of rites in Beijing.

sentences.zh: 三十八年，授文淵閣大學士。

translations.literal: In the thirty-eighth year he was appointed Grand Secretary of the Hall of Literary Depth.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 38 he became grand secretary of the Hall of Literary Depth.

sentences.zh: 三十九年，琇入覲，訟父受誣。

translations.literal: In the thirty-ninth year, when Xiu came to audience, he sued on behalf of his father, saying he had been slandered.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 39, when Guo Xiu came to audience, he sued on behalf of his father, claiming slander.

sentences.zh: 上詰佛倫，自承不實，當奪官，援赦得免。

translations.literal: The Emperor questioned Folun; he himself confessed that it was not true and ought to lose office, but by invoking amnesty he was spared.
translations.idiomatic: Questioned by the Emperor, Folun admitted the charge was false and should have cost him his office, but was spared by amnesty.

sentences.zh: 未幾，以原品休致。

translations.literal: Before long he retired at his former rank.
translations.idiomatic: He soon retired at his former rank.

sentences.zh: 旋卒。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died soon after.

sentences.zh: 論曰：康熙中，滿洲大臣以權位相尚者，惟索額圖、明珠，一時氣勢熏灼，然不能終保令名，卒以貪侈敗。

translations.literal: The commentary says: In the Kangxi reign, among Manchu great ministers who vied in power and position, only Songgotu and Mingzhu—for a time their aura blazed hot—yet they could not preserve a good name to the end and finally fell through greed and extravagance.
translations.idiomatic: Commentary: In the Kangxi era, among Manchu ministers who rivaled one another for power, only Songgotu and Mingzhu briefly blazed with influence, yet neither kept a good name and both fell to greed and excess.

sentences.zh: 索額圖以附皇太子得罪，禍延於後嗣。

translations.literal: Songgotu was punished for attaching himself to the Crown Prince, and calamity extended to his descendants.
translations.idiomatic: Songgotu was ruined for siding with the Crown Prince, and disaster reached his heirs.

sentences.zh: 明珠與索額圖競權，不附皇太子，雖被彈事罷相，聖祖猶念其贊撤籓，力全之，以視索額圖，豈不幸哉？

translations.literal: Mingzhu contended with Songgotu for power and did not attach himself to the Crown Prince; though impeached and removed from the chancellorship, the sage ancestor still remembered his support for withdrawing the fiefs and strove to preserve him—compared with Songgotu, was he not more fortunate?
translations.idiomatic: Mingzhu competed with Songgotu and refused the Crown Prince; though impeached and dismissed as chancellor, the Emperor still remembered his support for withdrawing the fiefs and protected him—was he not luckier than Songgotu?

sentences.zh: 若國柱、佛倫，則權門之疏附矣。

translations.literal: As for Guozhu and Folun, they were but distant hangers-on of the power-holders.
translations.idiomatic: Yuguo and Folun, by contrast, were mere hangers-on of the powerful.
